newsitem.title: GERMANY: Soy campaigners target oil mills, legislators.
newsitem.headline: Soy campaigners target oil mills, legislators.

text.p: German consumer and environmentalist groups on Tuesday asked European oilseeds processors and legislators to help their campaign for curbs on genetically altered grains.

"Seed crushers have a key function in resisting U.S. attempts to introduce biotechnology in European food," Greenpeace campaigner Joerg Naumann told a news conference ahead of the arrival of a ship that probably has modified soybeans aboard.
"It is possible to separate new soybeans from traditional ones and U.S. sources tell us there are now beans available which are guaranteed to be free of genetic manipulation," he said.
"But seed crushers refuse to tell us what they are buying, where it is going, and whether they will offer unmodified soya products separately. They're destroying their own market."
Developed by Monsanto Co of the U.S., the soybeans have been made resistant to a widely-used weedkiller.
Lobbyists plan to step up pressure on legislators in Bonn and Brussels to ensure consumers are informed about the origin of food on the label.
"Current provisions are unsatisfactory and private sector controls are not good enough to protect consumers," said Dan Leskien of BUND, German affiliate of Friends of the Earth.
A committee seeeking to find a compromise on labelling of so-called novel foods between the European Parliament and the EU Commission had no plans to label soya products.
The Bonn government said food laws should be deregulated and was playing into the hands of the industry, Leskien said.
According to a survey conducted for Greenpeace by Emnid, a Munich-based research institute, 73 percent of German consumers would avoid genetically-modified soybean products for now.
Some 87 percent advocate boycotting firms using them without proper labelling.
German Social Democrat MP Liesel Hartenstein issued a statement accusing the government of ignoring consumer health concerns.
"Consumers must not be degraded into guinea pigs," she said. She demanded a segregation of new and traditional soybeans, strict labelling and research assessing health risks from transgenic food.
